title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, pages 94-97 of the 1986 'Ateliers' notes. The objects are 'dispositions' E: a set E with a symmetric relation x|o|y (read here as orthogonality or separation). Each E has an associated complete lattice Σ_E of 'closed' subsets (sets equal to their double polar, i.e. ideals for the polarity), with closure Ψ°_E. On p. 94 a correspondence E → E' is a relation α: E → Σ_{E'} (equivalently R ⊂ E×E') satisfying conditions a) and b). On p. 95 these are shown to be in bijection with sup-preserving maps α_*: Σ_E → Σ_{E'}, via α_*(S) = sup_{x∈S} α(x).

This page (96), in modern terms:
(1) Composition is the closure of relational composition, β∘_dis α = sup Ψ°_{E''}(β∘_ens α). It is associative, and the identity on E is the closure of the diagonal, x ↦ Ψ°_E(x).
(2) The category of dispositions with these correspondences is equivalent to the category of 'espaces' (Grothendieck also floats the name 'topocosmos'), namely the complete lattices Σ_E with maps preserving arbitrary sups. A sup-map is what is meant by a 'correspondence' between espaces. This is a full subcategory of Sup, the category of complete lattices and sup-maps.
(3) This category is canonically equivalent to its opposite by an involutive 'autoduality'. It is the identity on objects and sends a morphism to its transpose: the correspondence R goes to tR. In lattice terms, f ↦ f† = ⊥∘f_*∘⊥, where f_* is the right adjoint of f and ⊥ is the polar orthocomplement, which is an order-reversing involution of Σ_E. In modern language this is a dagger structure, an identity-on-objects involutive contravariant functor.
(4) In a bracket he draws an explicit analogy with Hilbert spaces and, more generally, vector spaces with a self-duality, where this involution is the adjoint operator.
(5) He announces open questions inspired by trivial dispositions (where Σ_E = P(E) and correspondences are ordinary relations). The next page asks whether Hom(E,E') is itself an 'espace', namely the one of a product disposition E×E' with (x,x')|o|(y,y') iff x|o|y or x'|o|y'. That is the internal-hom / tensor question.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The autoduality uses the symmetry of the relation |o|: polar closure then gives an order-reversing involution ⊥ on Σ_E, and f ↦ ⊥∘(right adjoint of f)∘⊥ is a well-defined identity-on-objects involution. Without symmetry the dual object would be a different lattice; this is implicit, not stated.
Associativity of the closed composition is asserted rather than proved here. It follows from the equivalence with sup-maps, whose composition is ordinary composition.

The claimed equivalence is with the full subcategory of Sup whose objects are the lattices of closed sets of such polarities, i.e. complete ortholattices. Grothendieck's description 'applications croissantes qui commutent aux sup quelconques' is correct for that subcategory.

ideas.what: Category of orthogonality spaces (dispositions) with correspondences composed by closure of relational composition, equivalent to complete (ortho)lattices with sup-preserving maps
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality spaces / orthosets with sup-maps or Galois connections; full subcategory of Sup (quantale-enriched relations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (polarities, 1940); Foulis-Randall; Joyal-Tierney 1984 for Sup; Heunen-Jacobs 2010; Paseka-Vetterlein ~2020-22 for categories of orthogonality spaces

ideas.what: Identity-on-objects involutive self-duality given by transposing correspondences (f ↦ ⊥∘f_*∘⊥), explicitly compared to adjoint operators on Hilbert spaces
ideas.modern_name: Dagger category structure; dagger categories of orthomodular lattices / orthosets (dagger kernel categories)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Selinger 2007 (dagger categories); Heunen-Jacobs 2010 (OMLatGal as a dagger kernel category); Jacobs 2010; Paseka-Vetterlein

ideas.what: Open question whether correspondences E → E' form an 'espace' attached to a product disposition E×E' with the 'or' orthogonality
ideas.modern_name: Internal hom / tensor product of orthogonality spaces (*-autonomy of Sup restricted to ortholattices); tensor-product problem in quantum logic
ideas.usually_credited_to: Foulis-Randall, Aerts (non-existence of good tensor products of orthomodular lattices); Joyal-Tierney / Barr (*-autonomous Sup)

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck explicitly identifies the identity-on-objects transposition involution on the category of orthogonality spaces (complete ortholattices with sup-maps) as an analogue of Hilbert-space adjoints. This is a dagger-category viewpoint on orthogonality spaces, independently developed in categorical quantum logic only after 2007-2010 (Heunen-Jacobs, Paseka-Vetterlein). He apparently does not link it to quantum logic, but the structure is the same.
missed.quote: canoniquement équivalente à la catégorie opposée, par une "autodualité" (involutive) qui est l'identité sur les objets ... la flèche transposée [Analogie avec les espaces de Hilbert, ... et les opérateurs adjoints...]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and motivation for dagger structures on orthosets. His 'disposition' framework may offer a combinatorial, relation-based presentation of these categories.

missed.claim: Open question (continued on p. 97) whether the correspondences E → E' are exactly the closed sets of the product disposition E×E' with (x,x')|o|(y,y') iff x|o|y or x'|o|y'. He suspects this fails except for trivial dispositions, and then asks whether Hom is an 'espace' at all. This is the tensor/internal-hom problem for orthogonality spaces.
missed.quote: Questions ouvertes, que je ne vois pas encore tirer au clair, suggérées par le cas des dispositions triviales.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It connects to the known obstruction to tensor products of orthomodular lattices in quantum logic, and to closed/*-autonomous structure in categories of orthosets.

deep.surprise_reason: The equivalence with Sup and the adjoint-based self-duality are classical lattice theory. But Grothendieck's explicit 1986 framing as an identity-on-objects involution analogous to Hilbert-space adjoints anticipates the dagger-category treatment of orthogonality spaces later developed in categorical quantum logic, and it is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'composition est associative, avec comme identités', not 'composition et association, avec les/comme l'identité'.
Identity formula: 'T_E = sup Ψ°_E ∘ id_E' (closure of the diagonal), not 'sm Π^0_E'.
'La catégorie des dispositions et correspondances entre telles', not 'dérivateurs'.
'disposants commutatifs [?]' and 'ou espaces (ou "topocosmos"?)'; read 'espaces' rather than 'topos'.
'prenant comme morphismes les applications croissantes qui commutent aux sup quelconques', not 'en sens quelconque'.
Insertion reads '(définissant une "correspondance" entre les espaces)', not 'entre les topos'.
'suggérées par le cas des dispositions triviales', not 'inspirées par le cas des dérivateurs triviaux'.
